en-US.shortDescription: Remembers who in the house said what, when, and whether it still holds.
en-US.fullDescription:
Alexa+ takes actions now, not just answers, and that changes what goes wrong. A wrong answer is annoying. A wrong action is a breach of trust.

A home is the hardest place to get this right, because household state is contested. Several people, competing preferences, different authority, and facts that quietly expire. Dad set the thermostat rule. The kid overrode it. Someone was ill last week. You changed coffee in March.

Hearth gives Alexa+ a household memory with the three things ordinary memory leaves out. Provenance: every preference records who said it, when, and in what situation, so it is never just “thermostat at 19” but “Dad, three weeks ago, during the cold snap”. Supersession: preferences are retired rather than overwritten, so you can ask what the house used to think and when it changed its mind. Contest resolution: when two people disagree, Hearth resolves by authority and recency and then explains the resolution instead of silently picking one.

On top sits an action ledger. Every autonomous action is recorded against the exact preferences that justified it, so “why did you do that” has a real answer. Retire one preference out loud and the behaviour changes, with no app and no settings screen.

Situations end, too. “Gran has gone home” closes everything that was only true while she was staying, without anyone having to remember what those things were.
